annotations.title: Imports and Module Header: Unified Ptolemy Framework
annotations.content:
The three imports bring together the mathematical ingredients: `PtolemysComplexProof` provides the complex Ptolemy inequality (‖z₁-z₃‖·‖z₂-z₄‖ ≤ ‖z₁-z₂‖·‖z₃-z₄‖ + ‖z₂-z₃‖·‖z₁-z₄‖ for any z_i ∈ ℂ); `PtolemysTheoremOQ01OQ02` provides the spherical Ptolemy equality (for concyclic unit-sphere points) and the chord-arc identity (‖a-b‖ = 2·sin(arccos(⟨a,b⟩)/2)); `Mathlib.Analysis.Complex.Trigonometric` provides `Real.sinh` for the hyperbolic case.

The module header explains the curvatureSin framework: a single function parametrised by curvature K that recovers sin (K=1), the identity (K=0), and sinh (K=-1). This is the `sn_K` function from the differential geometry of surfaces of constant curvature. The module's main new result — `spherical_ptolemy_ineq_curvatureSin` — proves the Ptolemy inequality unconditionally for unit-circle points in ℂ, whereas the equality requires concyclicity. The proof chain (chord-arc → express sin as ‖·‖/2 → Ptolemy inequality / 4) is spelled out in full.
annotations.mathContext: The curvatureSin schema: $\text{sn}_K(t) = \begin{cases} \sin(\sqrt{K}\cdot t)/\sqrt{K} & K > 0 \\ t & K = 0 \\ \sinh(\sqrt{|K|}\cdot t)/\sqrt{|K|} & K < 0 \end{cases}$. The unified Ptolemy equality: $\text{sn}_K(d_{ac}/2) \cdot \text{sn}_K(d_{bd}/2) = \text{sn}_K(d_{ab}/2) \cdot \text{sn}_K(d_{cd}/2) + \text{sn}_K(d_{ad}/2) \cdot \text{sn}_K(d_{bc}/2)$ for cyclic quadrilaterals in $\kappa$-geometry.

annotations.title: curvatureSin: Unified Trigonometric Function for κ-Geometry
annotations.content:
The definition uses two nested `if-then-else` branches to handle the three cases: K=0 (identity), K>0 (spherical), K<0 (hyperbolic). The `noncomputable` modifier is required because Real.sin and Real.sqrt involve transcendental computations.

For K>0: `sin(√K · t) / √K`. For K=1, this gives sin(t)/1 = sin(t). The factor 1/√K is the normalisation ensuring sn_K(0) = 0 and d/dt[sn_K(t)]|_{t=0} = 1 for all K, which is the key property making sn_K the 'right' generalisation.

For K<0: `sinh(√|K| · t) / √|K|` — note `Real.sqrt (-K)` since K<0 makes -K>0. For K=-1 this gives sinh(t)/1 = sinh(t).

For K=0: the identity t. This is the L'Hôpital limit: as K→0, sin(√K·t)/√K → t (applying L'Hôpital with respect to K). The piecewise definition makes this limit exact at K=0.
annotations.mathContext: $\text{sn}_K(t) = \begin{cases} \sin(\sqrt{K} t)/\sqrt{K} & K > 0 \\ t & K = 0 \\ \sinh(\sqrt{-K} t)/\sqrt{-K} & K < 0 \end{cases}$. Normalization: $\frac{d}{dt}\text{sn}_K(t)\big|_{t=0} = 1$ for all $K$.

annotations.title: Basic Properties: curvatureSin 0=id, 1=sin, -1=sinh, always 0 at t=0
annotations.content:
Six lemmas establish the fundamental special cases. `curvatureSin_zero` and `curvatureSin_zero_right` are tagged `@[simp]` for automatic rewriting — the first handles K=0 (identity case), the second handles t=0 (all geometries agree at origin).

`curvatureSin_pos` and `curvatureSin_neg` are helper lemmas exposing the formulas for K>0 and K<0 respectively, proved by `simp only` with the `if_neg` and `if_pos` lemmas. These are used inside `curvatureSin_one` and `curvatureSin_neg_one`.

`curvatureSin_one` is the critical instance: `rw [curvatureSin_pos one_pos, Real.sqrt_one, one_mul, div_one]` rewrites sin(√1·t)/√1 → sin(1·t)/1 → sin(t)/1 → sin(t) in four steps.

`curvatureSin_neg_one` handles K=-1: `rw [curvatureSin_neg (by norm_num : (-1:ℝ) < 0)]`, then uses `have h : -(-1:ℝ) = 1 := by norm_num` to simplify √(-(-1)) = √1 = 1.

annotations.title: Spherical Ptolemy Equality in curvatureSin 1 Language
annotations.content:
This section introduces the variable `{V : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup V] [InnerProductSpace ℝ V]` for a real inner product space, making the result work for any dimension (unit sphere in ℝⁿ). The theorem `spherical_ptolemy_eq_curvatureSin` states the Ptolemy equality: for four concyclic unit-sphere points a,b,c,d with diagonals meeting at p (angles ∠apC = ∠bpd = π, i.e., p is the intersection), curvatureSin 1 satisfies the Ptolemy equality.

The proof is a one-liner: `simp only [curvatureSin_one]` replaces all curvatureSin 1 with sin, then `exact SphericalPtolemy.spherical_ptolemy h_cosph h_apc h_bpd ha hb hc hd` applies the imported result directly. This demonstrates the power of the curvatureSin framework: restating existing results in the unified language requires only the curvatureSin_one lemma.

**Concyclicity is essential**: the equality requires `Cospherical ({a,b,c,d})` and the angle conditions `∠ a p c = π`, `∠ b p d = π`. Without these, only the inequality holds.
annotations.mathContext: Spherical Ptolemy equality for concyclic $a,b,c,d$ on unit sphere: $\text{sn}_1(d_{ac}/2) \cdot \text{sn}_1(d_{bd}/2) = \text{sn}_1(d_{ab}/2) \cdot \text{sn}_1(d_{cd}/2) + \text{sn}_1(d_{ad}/2) \cdot \text{sn}_1(d_{bc}/2)$, where $d_{ij} = \arccos(\langle a_i, a_j \rangle)$.

annotations.title: Spherical Ptolemy Inequality: Main New Result — No Concyclicity Needed
annotations.content:
The main new contribution: `spherical_ptolemy_ineq_curvatureSin` proves the Ptolemy INEQUALITY for ANY four unit-circle points z₁,z₂,z₃,z₄ ∈ ℂ with ‖z_i‖=1, without requiring them to be concyclic.

The proof is a six-step calculation:
1. `simp only [curvatureSin_one]` — reduces to sin.
2. Six applications of `SphericalPtolemy.unit_sphere_chord_via_sin` give chord-arc identities: ‖z_i-z_j‖ = 2·sin(arccos(⟨z_i,z_j⟩_ℝ)/2).
3. Six `linarith` calls invert each chord-arc identity: sin(arccos(⟨z_i,z_j⟩_ℝ)/2) = ‖z_i-z_j‖/2.
4. Six `rw` calls substitute these into the goal.
5. Algebraic simplification: `ring` rewrites ‖·‖/2 * ‖·‖/2 = ‖·‖·‖·‖/4.
6. `linarith` from `hP := ptolemy_inequality z₁ z₂ z₃ z₄` (divide by 4).

The key insight: the chord-arc identity converts the spherical metric (expressed via sin of half the arccos inner product) into Euclidean norms. Once in norm form, the complex Ptolemy inequality applies. The factor 4 cancellation is the bookkeeping.
annotations.mathContext: For $z_i \in \mathbb{C}$ with $\|z_i\| = 1$: chord-arc gives $\|z_i - z_j\| = 2 \sin(d_{ij}/2)$, so $\sin(d_{ij}/2) = \|z_i - z_j\|/2$. The goal becomes $(\|z_1-z_3\|/2)(\|z_2-z_4\|/2) \leq (\|z_1-z_2\|/2)(\|z_3-z_4\|/2) + (\|z_2-z_3\|/2)(\|z_1-z_4\|/2)$, which is $\text{ptolemy\_inequality}/4$.
